note: Thin lexical reference for the IP network case (an interfaces view against a topology view of one network). Identity-only entries; it records no relationships and names no instance. It has NO entry for identifiers a system issues for itself (tp-id). A port and its name are distinct entries, as are a link bundle and a physical connection, so labels sharing 'interface' or 'link' bind apart.

entries.label: network device
entries.definition: One piece of network equipment that forwards traffic and owns ports.

entries.label: physical port
entries.definition: One physical attachment point on a device, where exactly one cable or fibre ends.

entries.label: link bundle
entries.definition: A logical interface on one device made of several of its physical ports acting as one.
entries.example: an aggregated Ethernet interface with two member ports

entries.label: bundle membership
entries.definition: The relation that says a physical port is one of the members of a link bundle on the same device.
entries.example: port 1 is a member of bundle 3

entries.label: physical connection
entries.definition: The fact that two physical ports on different devices are joined by one cable or fibre.
entries.example: the cable from port 1 of router X to port 2 of router Y

entries.label: nominal speed
entries.definition: The nominal transmission speed of a port or of the connection it ends, with its unit.

entries.label: hardware address
entries.definition: The hardware address burned into a physical port.

entries.label: IP address
entries.definition: An IP address configured on a port or bundle.

entries.label: router identifier
entries.definition: The routing identifier of a device.

entries.label: device-issued interface name
entries.definition: The name that the device itself gives a port or bundle; unique only within that device.

entries.label: interface index
entries.definition: A device-local integer index of an interface; arbitrary and unique only within that device.

entries.label: topology
entries.definition: A set of devices and connections managed together as one network.
